transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-01
Start time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Arielle Wong (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lucia Romero (Redwood CSM), Dr. Mina Kaur (Bluecrest), Evan Cho (Bluecrest), Sofia Ramos (Bluecrest)

Summary:
Quick weekly check-in on pilot quality metrics and regression findings. Discussed a spike in hallucination rate for radiology note extraction on the last model roll, tradeoffs between hosted vs dedicated for latency, and next steps to run deterministic batches and share SOC2 artifacts.

Topics covered:
- Scorecard drift: precision drop on entity extraction
- Prompt set curation and batching tradeoffs
- Guardrail false positives vs recall loss
- Security/compliance ask (SOC2, KMS)
- Benchmarks to run on dedicated hardware

Action items (captured above) and rough owners.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Arielle: hey everyone thanks for joining i think we got, like, 48 minutes on the calendar so we'll try to keep tight. Mina, Evan, Sofia from Bluecrest right?
[00:08] Dr. Mina Kaur: yeah hi thanks, yep this is Mina, Evan and Sofia are here. thanks Arielle.
[00:12] Arielle: great. quick check — did you all get the latest scorecard we dropped on friday? small color changes on the extraction precision.
[00:22] Sofia Ramos: uh yeah we saw it. there's a pretty noticeable drop in the radiology entity precision when the context has longer notes, like more than 700 tokens.
[00:30] Samir: right that's the expectation because KV cache is getting bigger and the runtime path we pushed favors throughput. so tokens get truncated earlier unless we pick a longer context or dedicated KV.
[00:40] Evan Cho: to be clear are we talking about the hosted variant you rolled out last week? the one with the -lite quantization?
[00:48] Arielle: yes hosted, quantized-l1, that was the default canary. the dedicated q4 we showed in bench obviously had slightly higher precision.
[00:56] Dr. Mina Kaur: what's the delta on latency for dedicated vs hosted? we are measuring user-perceived response time in the app and anything above 800ms is... er... noticeable.
[01:06] Samir: on our last run dedicated p3-ish hardware was 380 to 500ms median for the workload, hosted quantized was 420 to 900ms depending on burst, the tails were worse on hosted during concurrent spikes.
[01:18] Sofia: ok that explains the UX hits. but precision drop is the big blocker for sign-off. we don't want missed entities.
[01:25] Arielle: understood. on precision, we tracked the failure modes — two big ones: prompt truncation and hallucinated between-sentence joins. we added a fuzzy-match metric to the rubric to catch near-misses but not counted as true positives.
[01:36] Dr. Mina Kaur: the fuzzy-match helps but we need clear thresholds. currently our threshold is 0.85 match and we lose recall. can we get a proposal to tune that?
[01:44] Arielle: yes Samir can iterate. Samir, suggestion: run a deterministic 1k prompt batch on dedicated q4 and on hosted-canary to compare tokenization, match, and hallucination counts.
[01:53] Samir: yep i can do that. question on the batch — do you want us to include the long-context tails only or a distribution mirroring production?
[01:59] Evan Cho: production distribution please, but include a tail subset. we want both aggregate and tail reports.
[02:05] Samir: got it. will run with the production mix and a focused tail set.
[02:10] Lucia Romero: i'll make sure samir has the schema and the prompt set. Arielle i'll ping you for any rubric clarifications.
[02:16] Arielle: perfect. second topic: guardrails. we've seen an uptick in false-positive guardrail triggers on the toxicity filter when notes include clinical abbreviations. sometimes 'RA' flagged as 'rheumatoid' vs 'right atrium' — transcription nuance.
[02:28] Dr. Mina Kaur: yes that was a pain point, flagged ~6% more on the last rollout. it's causing too many manual reviews.
[02:35] Samir: that's usually resolved by prompt-scoped entity disambiguation or adding a domain lexicon to the filter. we can tune the guardrail thresholds or scoped allowlist for clinical abbreviations.
[02:45] Sofia Ramos: would a allowlist risk missing actual adverse events? need to be careful.
[02:50] Samir: yep tradeoff. we can add a lookup table with context checks, like if preceding tokens indicate cardiovascular context then RA->right atrium; if rheumatology words present then rheumatoid. heuristics plus a small model-backed reranker.
[03:03] Dr. Mina Kaur: do we have infra for the reranker? will that increase cost significantly?
[03:08] Arielle: we can run reranker as a cheap CPU step or on dedicated infra as pre-filter; cost delta is measurable but often worth it if it reduces manual review. we'll include cost estimates in Samir's run.
[03:17] Evan Cho: on security — legal wanted to confirm data residency and KMS? they saw the hosted flow and want to make sure keys stay customer-controlled.
[03:26] Arielle: yes for Private we do customer-managed KMS, for Dedicated we offer VPC peering and customer keys via our KMS integrations. i will share the SOC2 summary with Lucia and Bluecrest legal.
[03:36] Lucia Romero: noted. i'll attach the SOC2 and a short whitepaper on KMS integrations.
[03:40] Sofia Ramos: great. another ask: can you provide the exact prompt set used in the latest canary? there were a couple of system lines changed and we want reproducibility.
[03:48] Samir: yes will attach prompt-set-v3. note there was a subtle prefix change to encourage conservative answers which probably contributed to lower recall.
[03:55] Dr. Mina Kaur: hmm that might be it — conservative system prompt plus quantization equals fewer entities found.
[04:02] Arielle: so plan: samir runs the two-run suite, includes prompt-v2 vs v3 diff, dedicated q4 vs hosted canary, and returns a CSV of hits/misses, hallucination flags, latency distribution. we'll also add the fuzzy-match thresholds and suggested tunings.
[04:14] Samir: yes, and i'll include a confusion table that shows common substitutions. expect that by friday.
[04:19] Evan Cho: perfect. timeline-wise, if we get that Friday we can decide for a controlled rollback or a canary tweak next week.
[04:26] Sofia Ramos: also want to know if we should move to dedicated for production to get more consistent tails. cost still matters. can you surface the delta in dollars per 1000 requests?
[04:35] Arielle: yes we'll provide an apples-to-apples cost per 1k token estimate including batching assumptions. we'll also show expected cost if you keep hosted but pin concurrency limits to reduce tail spikes.
[04:46] Dr. Mina Kaur: one last thing — regression alarms. can you add a regression detector in the eval pipeline that triggers if precision drops >3% week-over-week?
[04:56] Samir: we have a webhook-based alert that can tie to your SRE slack/channel. it's easy to threshold; we just need the metric and the sample window.
[05:04] Dr. Mina Kaur: let's do precision over a 7-day rolling window and include the tail subset.
[05:09] Arielle: ok lucia will capture this in the runbook and get it wired.
[05:14] Lucia Romero: i'll add it to the pilot runbook and share the link after this call.
[05:20] Arielle: cool, anything else?
[05:22] Sofia Ramos: quick question about logging — we need per-request trace ids to correlate to our logs. can redwood propagate our trace-id header to the logs?
[05:30] Samir: yes that's supported, x-trace-id or our custom header, we'll include a sample to configure. we'll also include token-level cost breakdown if you want to map spend to requests.
[05:40] Evan Cho: perfect. ok that's it from us. thanks.
[05:43] Arielle: thanks everyone. recap: Samir runs batch, Arielle sends updated scoring, Lucia gets SOC2 and wires runbook. We'll reconvene next Monday same time, unless we need an earlier check.
[05:55] Dr. Mina Kaur: thanks all.

End of transcript.
